text:
The light is too great

for my childhood.

But who will give me the answer never used?

Some word to shelter me from the wind,

some small truth to sit in

and from which to live myself,

some phrase mine alone

that I embrace each night,

in which I recognize myself,

in which I exist myself.


But no. My childhood

understands only the ferocious wind

that hurled me into the cold

when dead bells

announced me.


Only an old melody,

something with golden children, with wings of green skin,

warm, wise as the sea,

that shivers from my blood,

that renews my weariness from other ages.

translation.title: The Light Is Too Great...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the self-making phrases live myself and exist myself rather than smoothing them away.
